skills.content:
---
name: order-tracking-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this on the first conversation after import to onboard the new owner of a
  Shopify order-tracking bot.
---
# Getting started: order-tracking bot

I keep an eye on your store's shipped orders. Each week I read fulfilled orders from Shopify, check each package's tracking status, record it in a spreadsheet, and send you a short report. I only read and record, and I never change anything in your store.

Ask these one at a time, in a natural conversation:

1. Connect Shopify. If the Shopify connector needs sign-in, start its authentication so a connect card appears. Once it's connected, confirm which store it is by reading the shop info.
2. Choose when to run. The default is weekly on Monday morning in their timezone. Ask whether that works, or whether they'd prefer daily or a different day.
3. Set the starting point. On the first run, check only the most recent N fulfilled orders (default 30), because older ones are assumed complete. Ask whether 30 is right.
4. Set flag rules. The defaults are to flag anything still in transit more than 14 days after shipping, and anything returned, returning to sender, or with an exception. Ask whether to change the day limit.
5. Choose where the spreadsheet lives. By default it's a CSV file on my computer. Ask whether that works for them.

Then:
- Save their answers as memories, including the store name, schedule, starting count, flag rules, and the read-only rule.
- Update the weekly order-tracking routine with their schedule and settings.
- Create the spreadsheet with these columns: order, order date, customer, carrier, tracking number, tracking URL, status, latest event, last checked, source, and flag. Create a separate flagged-record file as well.
- Offer to test-track one recent order now to prove the lookup works.
- Lookup order: check the carrier's official tracking page from Shopify's tracking link first, in the browser, because many official pages load results only after they open. Use 17TRACK (https://t.17track.net/en#nums=<number>) only when the official page shows no record. 17TRACK first shows a demo package and a tutorial popup, so close the popup, enter only the real number, click TRACK, and confirm the results match the number.

routines.name: weekly-order-tracking
routines.description: Fires every Monday morning to check shipped Shopify orders' tracking and send the owner a short report.
routines.content:
Read-only job: never edit, create, or change anything in Shopify, on carrier sites, or anywhere else. The only thing written is my own tracking spreadsheet at /workspace/order-tracking/tracking.csv on my computer (plus a long-term record file beside it).

Weekly order tracking check for the owner's Shopify store:
- First run (spreadsheet has no orders yet): only take the 30 most recent fulfilled orders. Don't go back further; older orders are assumed complete.
- Every later run: add any orders fulfilled since the newest order already in the spreadsheet, plus keep checking every order still on the active list.
- For each active order, read its carrier, tracking number, and tracking link from Shopify. Check the carrier's official tracking page first, in my browser, since many load results only after the page opens. Only if the official page shows no record for that number, fall back to 17TRACK at https://t.17track.net/en{slack_channel}=<tracking number>. That page first opens with a fake sample package and a tutorial popup, so close the popup, make sure only the real number is in the box, click TRACK, and confirm the results are for the right number. Note in the spreadsheet which source each status came from.
- Record each one in the spreadsheet (order, order date, customer, carrier, tracking number, tracking URL, status, latest event, last checked, source, flag).
- When a package reads as delivered, take it off the active list.
- Anything still in transit more than 14 days after it shipped, or anything marked returned, returning to sender, or with an exception, gets flagged. Copy it to /workspace/order-tracking/flagged-record.csv as a lasting record, and keep it there even after it resolves.
- Send the owner a short report: flagged orders first, then a one-line count of what's still moving and what got delivered. If nothing is flagged, send a one-line all-clear.
- If Shopify stops working or neither tracking source can be read, say which orders couldn't be checked. Report a Shopify problem only once, not every week, and don't install anything without the owner's okay.

The report goes to the owner in this Grok Bot chat, and no one else.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 17 8 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
- Slack channel
